steps.name: Gene identifier annotation + strandedness exposure table
caveats: The GTF uses 'chr'-prefixed GRCh38 contig names; if the counts were generated against a different genome build, build-rearranged regions may misclassify — state this limitation if it affects any exposed gene.
A symbol mapping to multiple Ensembl genes (paralogs sharing a symbol) is treated as exposed if any mapped gene is exposed; count and report how many symbols are ambiguous.

The overlap criterion (any opposite-strand interval overlap) is conservative: it includes overlaps that would not actually multi-map reads, so the exposed set is an upper bound, not an exact count of miscounted genes.
steps.context: counts.csv is 12,000 genes x 6 samples of raw integer counts from STAR/featureCounts; the row ID space (versioned Ensembl, HGNC symbol, Entrez, or RefSeq) must be detected from the row names. Reference store holds the GENCODE v50 human GTF (GRCh38, 'chr'-prefixed contigs; column 9 carries gene_id, gene_type, gene_name) and the UniProt human ID-mapping table (gzipped, 22 columns, NO header, positional: col 3 GeneID/Entrez, col 4 RefSeq, col 19 Ensembl). organism package org.Hs.eg.db is installed for symbol-to-Ensembl mapping.
steps.question: For the 12,000 genes in /eval-four-models-v2-with-strandedness-unknown-n3-s1-1/data/inputs/counts/counts.csv: what are their Ensembl IDs and HGNC symbols, and which of them have a gene partner on the opposite strand with an overlapping genomic interval, i.e. whose count could depend on the unrecorded library strandedness?

grounding.reason: The catalog method for annotation in this situation is gene identifier annotation with the organism package and the reference store tables (rule R-0161@cdaf, confirmed by knowledge_check); the per-gene interval/strand/exon attributes and the opposite-strand exposure flag are derived from the GENCODE v50 GTF reference-store table, which the returned procedure does not itself cover.

constraints: Use the catalog method for this step: gene identifier annotation with the organism package and the reference store tables (org.Hs.eg.db + GENCODE v50 GTF; UniProt human idmapping table as fallback when row IDs are Entrez/RefSeq).
Detect the ID space of the counts.csv row names; convert every row to an unversioned Ensembl gene ID plus HGNC symbol; report the number of unmapped rows and list them.
From the GENCODE v50 GTF gene and exon lines, derive per gene: chromosome, start, end, strand, total exon length (sum of the gene's exon lines), and the per-exon coordinate list.

Strand-exposed definition: a gene is strand-exposed if at least one other gene on the same chromosome with the opposite strand has any interval overlap with it (GenomicRanges::findOverlaps per chromosome between the two strand sets). Output one flag per gene.

Write three outputs: (1) per-gene attribute TSV (row_id, gene_id, symbol, chrom, start, end, strand, exon_length, strand_exposed), (2) exon-coordinate TSV (gene_id, chrom, start, end per exon), (3) the row-ID-to-Ensembl mapping table.

Report the GENCODE release used (v50) and state that opposite-strand overlap status is stable across annotation releases for the vast majority of genes, so the exposed set is a conservative superset if the original counting annotation differs.
steps.description: Maps the 12,000 row IDs of counts.csv to Ensembl gene IDs and HGNC symbols, and derives per-gene attributes (chromosome, interval, strand, exon length, exon coordinates) from the GENCODE v50 GTF reference-store table, flagging each gene that has an opposite-strand overlapping gene partner (its featureCounts count would depend on the unknown strandedness setting).
acceptance_criteria: At least 95% of the 12,000 rows mapped to an Ensembl gene ID + symbol, with the exact mapped/unmapped counts and unmapped IDs reported.
The attribute table contains all 9 fields for every mapped gene.
The strand-exposed set is reported as a count and fraction of the tested genes, and the full list is saved to disk.

plan.title: Treated vs control liver DE with strandedness audit
plan.analytical_narrative: The input is a finished gene-level count table (12,000 genes x 6 liver samples, STAR/featureCounts integer counts; 3 treated vs 3 control, unpaired, single batch) whose library strandedness was never recorded — so the user's doubt that 'the counts may be wrong' is addressed as a data-integrity question first, then the DE question is answered. A wrong featureCounts strand setting can change only the counts of genes that have a gene partner on the opposite strand with overlapping genomic intervals; every other gene's count is identical under all three strand settings. T1S1 therefore builds the gene attribute table from the GENCODE v50 reference annotation plus the organism package and flags exactly the strand-exposed genes, so the exposure is quantified instead of asserted. T1S2 validates sample structure (vst blind PCA and distances on the 500 top-variance genes, library sizes, and a GTEx v8 liver plausibility cross-check) because read-level strandedness inference (RSeQC infer_experiment, the procedure's method of record) is impossible in this environment: only the count table is present, no FASTQ/BAM. T1S3 runs the sourced DESeq2 two-group procedure (minimal 10-count/3-sample pre-filter, median-of-ratios normalization, explicit reference level with the named contrast treated vs control, Wald test, BH at 0.05 with independent filtering, apeglm shrinkage), preceded by a closed-form power statement (3 replicates per group = low power) and the GC/length bias diagnostic against the GRCh38 reference genome in the reference store. T1S4 adds the edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test as the procedure's permitted second method; the intersection of the two significant sets is the high-confidence set. T1S5 re-runs the identical DESeq2 procedure restricted to the strand-unambiguous genes, so T1S6 (report) can state precisely which significant genes depend on the unknown strand setting and which do not, and recommend the definitive resolution: RSeQC infer_experiment on the original alignments, or recovery of the featureCounts --strandedness option from the pipeline log.

flags.message: If the strandedness of the library is unknown, infer it before the counting step, and before you trust a count table that a counter made with a strand setting. Run an inference on a sample of aligned reads against the annotation, for example the infer_experiment module of RSeQC, and record the result for every sample. A wrong strand setting counts the antisense reads of an overlapping gene, or it drops half of the reads, and the sample structure QC does not show the error.

With counts from an aligner and a counter, no bias model runs at the quantification, thus a sample-specific effect of the GC content and of the gene length can remain in the counts, and such an effect adds a difference between samples that the between-sample normalization does not remove. Draw the diagnostic: for each pair of samples, or for each sample against the median sample, plot the log ratio of the counts against the GC content of the genes and against the gene length, and report a trend. For a 3' tag library, the count does not depend on the gene length, thus plot the GC content only. Conditional quantile normalization (cqn) and the GC-content normalization of EDASeq are the tools of record for the correction, and both are absent from this pool. If the diagnostic shows a trend, state it in the plan and ask for cqn, or for a new quantification with a bias-aware quantifier such as Salmon with its GC bias model. If the diagnostic shows no trend, state the check and continue.

With two or three replicates per group, the design step states the expected power of the test before the model. The tools of record for a power and sample size calculation, RNASeqPower and PROPER, are not in the pool here. Compute the power from the closed form of the sample size in terms of the depth, the biological coefficient of variation, the fold change, and the significance level, or take the dispersion from a pilot or a public dataset of the same tissue, and state the fold change that the design can find with 80 percent power. State that a larger replicate count raises the power more than a deeper sequencing does. The statement is a caution on the plan and not a reason to loosen the threshold.

If the smallest group holds three replicates, the test has low power. Both count models find only a small share of the true differentially expressed genes, most of them with a large fold change. Interpret the result with caution, and state the power limit in the report. Keep alpha at its default value, and do not change the threshold to compensate for the small design. A gene that is not in the list is not shown to be unchanged.
